task.description: Idiom/scope hard gate on commit 0f8bd06 (branch feature/WF03-ISS0056-20260818 vs origin/main) for ISS-0056's fix to lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex: loosened CHK-14 (check_unpermitted_edge_condition/1, renamed from check_non_gateway_condition_absence/1) permitting conditions on :HUMAN_TASK-sourced edges, plus new CHK-19 (check_human_task_fallback_edge/1) requiring a fallback edge on HUMAN_TASK nodes with a really-conditioned outgoing edge.
acceptance_criteria: Idiomatic pattern-matching/pipeline style consistent with rest of graph.ex
No abstraction/scope creep beyond ISS-0056 + validated design
Diff confined to lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex (plus docs/handoffs) -- lib/letflow/engine/ untouched

result.summary: Reviewed the full branch diff (git diff origin/main...HEAD) for lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex against ISS-0056, the validated design doc (lib/letflow/design/iss-0056-human-task-fallback-edge-validation.md), and ELIXIR-DEV's implementation report. Scope: confirmed via `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD -- lib/letflow/engine/` that lib/letflow/engine/ is completely untouched (empty diff) -- the run's hard scope boundary holds. The only code change is in lib/letflow/definitions/graph.ex; all other diff hunks are docs/handoffs artefacts (docs/issues/ISS-0056.yaml, handoffs/WF03-ISS0056-20260818/*, the design doc itself), which is expected process bookkeeping, not application-code scope creep. Idiom: the diff matches graph.ex's established style throughout -- check_unpermitted_edge_condition/1 keeps the same Enum.filter/Enum.map violation-building pipeline shape as its sibling CHK-13/15/16/17 checks; check_human_task_fallback_edge/1 filters graph.nodes to :HUMAN_TASK the same way check_gateway_condition_presence/1 (CHK-09-family) filters nodes, and correctly chooses a per-node Enum.filter+Enum.map (one violation per offending node) rather than reusing CHK-16's per-source-index grouping, since CHK-19's unit of concern is genuinely different (node, not edge) -- a real design choice, not a shortcut. The two new predicates (human_task_edge_really_conditioned?/1, human_task_edge_fallback_candidate?/1) are small, named, single-purpose functions rather than inlined boolean soup, consistent with the rest of the module. human_task_source?/3 is kept as a separate helper rather than folded into/generalizing exclusive_gateway_source?/3, deliberately preserving CHK-13/16's existing call sites untouched -- this is the right call for a fix scoped to CHK-14/CHK-19 only, not scope creep. No :gen_statem/supervision concerns apply to this pure validator module. Scope: nothing here exceeds ISS-0056 + the validated design -- CHK-13/15/17 are untouched as the design mandated, CHK-16's HUMAN_TASK gap (flagged by ISSUE-FIXER as optionally adjacent) was correctly NOT touched, matching the design's explicit deferral and avoiding creep. The disclosed, unreconciled inconsistency between human_task_edge_really_conditioned?/1 (non-trimming, deliberately mirrors transition.ex's really_conditioned?/1 literally per design doc) and blank_condition?/1 (trims) is intentional and documented in both the design doc and inline comments, not an oversight -- correctly not silently reconciled by ELIXIR-DEV, which would have been an undiscussed behavior change. Decision-record consistency: checked docs/migration/decisions/0001 through 0006 -- none constrain graph-validator internals; no conflict. docs/anti-patterns.md has no entries applicable to a pure-function validator change. Verified `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` exits 0 with no output (clean compile), corroborating ELIXIR-DEV's report. No type-safety gap worth a new docs/issues/ entry: the Violation.code union was correctly extended (:human_task_no_fallback_edge appended at the end, no reordering) rather than left as an untyped atom, so this change doesn't introduce a new unrepresentable-invalid-state class.
